title: 麦当劳在美规模化部署AI动态定价引擎，同城门店最高价差达21%
content:
McDonald's is accelerating the deployment of AI-based location-driven dynamic pricing engines in the US, marking a comprehensive deepening of artificial intelligence's application in physical retail pricing strategies. The system processes massive transaction data from over 13,000 company-owned stores and competitors like Wendy's to calculate optimal prices for each store.
This algorithm has led to significant price differences for the same products in the same area. For example, two McDonald's stores only two miles apart in Fresno, California, have a 21% difference in the price of a Big Mac (5.69 vs. 6.89 dollars), and the price difference in New York city stores also reaches 11%. To strengthen strategy implementation, McDonald's has made cooperating with AI pricing advisors a mandatory condition for franchise renewal starting January 2026.
This move reflects that AI dynamic pricing is rapidly spreading from service industries such as aviation and transportation to high-frequency traditional retail. Previously, retail giants had been continuously exploring algorithmic price adjustments based on user profiles. In 2019, Target used AI to track user locations for precise pricing, causing the price of the same Samsung TV to jump by $100 in the parking lot.
Currently, Walmart plans to install electronic price tags in all 4,600 stores across the US by the end of 2026. Its AI patents already have the capability to perform real-time differentiated pricing based on user browsing and purchasing behavior, although its management has recently pledged to limit such applications.
The differentiated pricing mechanism driven by AI algorithms is extending to offline physical commerce, significantly improving the digital monetization efficiency of the retail industry. However, while companies use model computing power to pursue profit maximization, how to balance the algorithm's black box and consumers' right to fair transactions has become an unavoidable compliance and trust challenge in the process of AI commercialization.

report.summary: 麦当劳在美万店上线AI动态定价，同城门店价差达21%
report.background: 动态定价并非新事物，航空、网约车、酒店早已广泛使用算法调价。近年来这套逻辑快速下沉到高频实体零售：2019年Target曾用AI追踪用户位置精准定价，同一台三星电视在停车场内涨价100美元。如今麦当劳将AI定价推进到超1.3万家自营门店，用海量交易数据与竞品（如Wendy's）数据为每家店算出最优价格，并把与AI定价顾问合作设为2026年1月起加盟续约的强制条件。沃尔玛计划2026年底前在全美4600家门店装上电子价签，其专利已具备按用户浏览与购买行为实时差异定价的能力。
key_points: 同城同品不同价已成现实：加州弗雷斯诺两家相距仅2英里的门店，巨无霸分别卖5.69和6.89美元，价差21%，纽约门店间价差也达11%。
定价依据不止门店成本，算法还抓取竞品数据与海量交易记录，为每家店单独计算“最优价格”，本质是把线上一人一价搬到线下。
麦当劳用加盟续约绑定AI定价顾问，意味着这不是试点而是制度化推行，加盟商的定价自主权被大幅压缩。
沃尔玛的电子价签可将调价从“按天”压缩到“按秒”，若真落地，消费者在线下也将面对和电商一样的实时浮动价格。
算法是黑箱，消费者难以知道此刻的价格为何比别人高，公平交易权与定价透明度的矛盾被放大。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这是动态定价从线上流量场走向线下物理世界的标志性案例，验证了算法在实体零售的变现效率，也会带动需求预测、计算机视觉客流分析、电子价签等一整条产业链。对开发者来说，定价系统涉及实时数据处理、竞品爬取、强化学习与合规审计，岗位与创业机会增加，但“可解释性”将成为硬性技术要求。对普通用户，同款商品同城不同价会越来越常见，比价难度和“被杀熟”的焦虑上升，也可能引发监管对算法定价的介入。
report.tools: 想跟进这一方向，可关注开源定价与优化工具 Google OR-Tools、Pyomo、Meta 的 Prophet 做需求预测；商业侧有 PROS、Revionics、Competera、Prisync 等定价 SaaS 与竞品价格监控；若关注合规，可研究模型可解释性工具 SHAP、LIME，以及电子价签方案商如 SoluM、Hanshow。
